sentences.en: I no longer believe in any other revolution, said Richard Wagner, save that which begins with the burning down of Paris.
sentences.zh: 我不再相信任何其他的革命，理查德·瓦格纳说，除了那场以烧毁巴黎为开端的革命。

sentences.en: A comment that speaks volumes about the outsized role that the French capital has played in the imaginings, not just of the French themselves, but of the entire world.
sentences.zh: 这段评论充分说明了这座法国首都不仅在法国人自己的想象中，而且在全世界的想象中都占据着举足轻重的地位。

sentences.en: And today's episode is the first episode of The Rest is History that we're devoting to the history of an entire city.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目是《一切皆历史》首度专门聚焦整座城市的历史。

sentences.en: And Dominic Zambra with me.
sentences.zh: 还有和我在一起的多米尼克·赞布拉。

sentences.en: It's got to be Paris, hasn't it, really?
sentences.zh: 非巴黎莫属，对吧，其实？

sentences.en: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think Paris has played this emblematic role, hasn't it, in the world's imagination for the best part of, well, certainly 500 years, maybe a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 我认为巴黎在世界想象中一直扮演着这种标志性的角色，嗯，至少有五百年，甚至一千年。

sentences.en: I actually don't like Paris at all, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，其实我一点也不喜欢巴黎。

sentences.en: As our Twitter followers will know.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的推特粉丝所知道的那样。

sentences.en: Yes, they do.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们知道。

sentences.en: Because every week, obviously, when we do an episode, we ask for questions.
sentences.zh: 因为显然，每周我们做节目时都会征集问题。

sentences.en: So mine, very francophile.
sentences.zh: 所以我的那个非常亲法。

sentences.en: We will be tracing the glories, beauties, wonders and terrors that have marked 2,000 years of the City of Light.
sentences.zh: 我们将追溯这座光之城两千年历史中的辉煌、美丽、奇迹与恐怖。

sentences.en: That was me.
sentences.zh: 那是我说的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Have you got mine there as well?
sentences.zh: 你那也有我的问题吗？

sentences.en: The City of Light?
sentences.zh: 光之城？

sentences.en: Or the most overrated city on Earth, awash in dog excrement where you often see people urinating in the streets.
sentences.zh: 还是地球上最被高估的城市，到处都是狗屎，经常能看到人们在街头随地小便。

sentences.en: I had the worst bout of food poisoning of my life in Paris, incidentally.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我在巴黎曾食物中毒，那是我一生中最糟糕的一次经历。

sentences.en: You took my voice perfectly.
sentences.zh: 你把我的声音模仿得惟妙惟肖。

sentences.en: You took my voice perfectly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你把我模仿得惟妙惟肖，汤姆。

sentences.en: John Bull Speaks.
sentences.zh: 约翰·布牛发话了。

sentences.en: I had scallops on Valentine's Day with my wife, and we both got hideously ill.
sentences.zh: 我和妻子在情人节吃了一顿扇贝，结果我们两个都病得不轻。

sentences.en: And that, to me, that was like the nail in the coffin of the City of Light.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这就好比是给光之城钉上了棺材板。

sentences.en: I haven't been back, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我再也没去过。

sentences.en: Never been back.
sentences.zh: 就再也没去过。

sentences.en: That's what comes of going abroad, though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不过，这就是出国旅游的代价，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, people used to take tins of bay beans, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们过去常常带一罐罐的药丸，对吧？

sentences.en: A terrible warning.
sentences.zh: 一个惨痛的警告。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank goodness, then.
sentences.zh: 那谢天谢地。

sentences.en: Thank goodness that, as well as the John Bull of Chipping Norton, we have our first French guest, Agnès Poirier,
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，除了来自齐平诺顿的约翰·布牛，我们还迎来了第一位法国嘉宾阿涅丝·普瓦里耶，

sentences.en: a well-known journalist, well-known commentator who is familiar to both French and to British listeners,
sentences.zh: 她是一位知名记者、知名评论员，法国和英国的听众对她都很熟悉，

sentences.en: but also has written two fantastic books on the history of Paris, Left Bank, Art, Passion, and the Rebirth of Paris, 1940 to 1950.
sentences.zh: 而且她还写了两本关于巴黎历史的精彩著作：《左岸：艺术、激情与巴黎的重生，1940-1950》。

sentences.en: And that's a really fabulous book because that 1940 to 1950, you get the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 那真是一本极好的书，因为在1940到1950年间，你经历第二次世界大战，

sentences.en: and then you get the recovery from the Second World War, and that's kind of an unusual way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后是二战后的复苏，这种切入角度相当别致。

sentences.en: And then, Agnès, Notre Dame, the soul of France, which obviously you wrote in the aftermath of the terrible fire that swept the great cathedral.
sentences.zh: 还有，阿涅丝，《巴黎圣母院：法国的灵魂》，显然你是在那座伟大教堂遭遇可怕大火后写下这本书的。

sentences.en: And you begin the book very movingly with an account of, you know, you watched the fire.
sentences.zh: 你在书中以非常感人的方式开篇，讲述了你目睹大火的经历。

sentences.en: You live right next to the cathedral itself.
sentences.zh: 你住的地方就紧挨着大教堂。

sentences.en: And that was something, the thought that Notre Dame might be lost was something that people in Paris, people in France obviously found incredibly upsetting,
sentences.zh: 那一刻，一想到巴黎人、法国人显然会感到无比沮丧的是巴黎圣母院可能会消失，

sentences.en: but also people around the world.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们也是如此。

sentences.en: And I wonder, why do you think it had the impact that it did, the thought that Notre Dame might be lost?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你认为“巴黎圣母院可能会消失”这一想法为什么会产生如此巨大的影响？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, yeah, we have to go back on that night, 15th of April, 2019, and I happened to be in Paris.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，是的，我们必须回到那个夜晚，2019年4月15日，当时我正好在巴黎。

sentences.en: And strangely, I was preparing to comment on an address that President Macron was going to do after the unrest of the yellow vest, the gilets jaunes.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，我当时正准备对马克龙总统在“黄马甲”骚乱后发表的讲话做评论。

sentences.en: And it was a beautiful, beautiful day.
sentences.zh: 那天天气好极了。

sentences.en: And when in Paris, I'm lucky to live right opposite on the left bank with a wonderful view on the south rose window.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎时我很幸运，就住在左岸的正对面，从厨房能将南面的玫瑰窗尽收眼底。

sentences.en: And 7pm, I see this huge smoke, yellow smoke and clouds through the kitchen window.
sentences.zh: 傍晚7点，我通过厨房窗户看到了这股巨大的浓烟，黄色的浓烟和云团。

sentences.en: And so I rush down on the quay, on the river bank, because it could only come from what is opposite, that is to say Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 于是我冲到河岸边的码头上，因为这只能来自正对面的地方，也就是巴黎圣母院。

sentences.en: And that was the beginning of a very dramatic evening.
sentences.zh: 那是一个极其戏剧性夜晚的开始。

sentences.en: And it's very strange, because there were two things happening at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这非常奇怪，因为当时有两件事同时发生。

sentences.en: You're a French person or a Parisian, and you feel this ontological shock, and you're profoundly upset, but you don't exactly know why.
sentences.zh: 作为一个法国人或巴黎人，你感受到了这种存在主义的冲击，你感到内心深受触动，但你又说不出个所以然来。

sentences.en: Of course, it's a gem of Gothic architecture.
sentences.zh: 当然，它是哥特式建筑的瑰宝。

sentences.en: And she's been with us, Notre Dame, for more than 850 years, achievement of humankind.
sentences.zh: 巴黎圣母院陪伴了我们八百五十多年，是人类文明的杰作。

sentences.en: But it went much further than that.
sentences.zh: 但它的意义远不止于此。

sentences.en: And that's why, actually, I wanted to write the book.
sentences.zh: 这也是我为什么要写这本书的原因。

sentences.en: I wanted to understand my own feelings.
sentences.zh: 我想理解我自己的感受。

sentences.en: And second shock is to see that the whole world is watching with us those images and feel the same thing.
sentences.zh: 第二个冲击是看到全世界都在和我们一起注视着这些画面，并感同身受。

sentences.en: And because I've got to commence, that's my daily job to, you know, everything, every time there's something happening in France or in Paris, I get calls from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 因为我需要做评论，这是我的日常工作，你知道，每当法国或巴黎发生什么事，我就会接到来自世界各地的电话。

sentences.en: And I need to find words immediately to explain what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我需要立即找到词汇来解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I had people in tears in TV studios and radio studios in Sydney, in Singapore, in Beijing, name it, all over the world.
sentences.zh: 悉尼、新加坡、北京，随便哪里，世界各地的电视和广播直播室里都有人在流泪。

sentences.en: And some of them, presenters, TV presenters in tears saying, and yes, I've never been to France, but I know Notre Dame, I'm in tears, explain why I felt like this.
sentences.zh: 其中一些电视节目主持人流着泪说：“阿涅丝，我从未去过法国，但我知道巴黎圣母院，我在哭泣，请解释一下为什么我有这种感觉。”

sentences.en: And so suddenly there was, I hadn't set foot in the cathedral in 15 years.
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，我已经15年没有踏进过大教堂了。

sentences.en: I'm not a practicing Catholic, I'm not religious.
sentences.zh: 我不是虔诚的天主教徒，我没有宗教信仰。

sentences.en: So the religious dimension, you know, couldn't tell the whole story.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道，宗教维度并不能说明全部问题。

sentences.en: And so we're really at the heart, if you like, of your podcast in, you know, why Paris?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你愿意的话，我们确实触及了你们播客的核心：为什么是巴黎？

sentences.en: Of course, Paris had to be the first podcast you would dedicate to a city, because this is the epitome of the city.
sentences.zh: 当然，巴黎理应成为你们专门为一座城市制作的首个播客的主角，因为这就是城市的缩影。

sentences.en: And I think it's been going on for a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这种情况已经持续了一千年。

sentences.en: And what do you think it means then, if you can boil it down?
sentences.zh: 那么如果你把它浓缩一下，你认为这意味着什么？

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, we're meant to be doing that in an hour, but if you can boil it down in sort of three lines or so, what is it that Paris represents, do you think?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然我们打算在一小时内讲完，但如果你能用大约三行字把它浓缩概括，你认为巴黎代表了什么？

sentences.en: It depends, you know, if we're starting in the 12th century, for instance, we could, especially if we're talking about Notre Dame,
sentences.zh: 这取决于，比如说如果我们从12世纪开始，我们可以，特别是如果我们谈论巴黎圣母院的话，

sentences.en: but we could also be slightly more modern or contemporary in the sense that I think for people today, they get their idea of Paris, because Paris is as much an idea than reality.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以更现代、更当代一些，因为我认为对于今天的人们来说，他们对巴黎有自己的看法，因为巴黎既是一个概念，也是一种现实。

sentences.en: But, you know, what's interesting, though, you talk about the medieval and the modern, but even in antiquity.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，你谈到了中世纪和现代，甚至在古代也是如此。

sentences.en: So there's a comment by Julian the Apostate, who was the nephew of Constantine the Great, and he says of Paris, so he calls it Lutetia, which is the Roman name,
sentences.zh: 背教者尤里安曾做过一番评论，他是君士坦丁大帝的侄子，他这样称呼巴黎，他称其为“卢泰西亚”，这是罗马时期的名字，

sentences.en: and he calls it my beloved Lutetia.
sentences.zh: 他称其为我挚爱的卢泰西亚。

sentences.en: So even in the Roman period, there was clearly something about it that gave it this kind of sense.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在罗马时期，它显然也有某种特质，赋予了它这种基调。

sentences.en: And I, perhaps, I don't know what it is, perhaps it's just the positioning of it on the scene, perhaps it's just kind of the drama of its positioning.
sentences.zh: 我可能，我不知道是什么，也许只是它在地理景观中的位置，也许只是它地理位置所带来的戏剧性。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: There's lots of cities on rivers.
sentences.zh: 有很多城市都依河而建。

sentences.en: I mean, there must be something more than that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一定还有比这更多的原因。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的。

sentences.en: Clearly, I mean, it's an important Roman city.
sentences.zh: 显然，它是一座重要的罗马城市。

sentences.en: Its name, Paris, comes from the local tribe, the Parisi.
sentences.zh: 它的名字“巴黎”（Paris）源自当地的一个部落——巴黎西族（Parisi）。

sentences.en: It survives the fall of Rome.
sentences.zh: 它在罗马灭亡后幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Kings in Paris, the Frankish kings, are building amphitheatres as late as the 6th century.
sentences.zh: 直到6世纪，巴黎的国王即法兰克国王仍在建造圆形剧场。

sentences.en: It's kind of amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太惊人了。

sentences.en: So in a sense, there's a kind of degree of continuity much greater than you get, say, in the history of London, where there really is a kind of meltdown.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，它具有某种程度的延续性，这比伦敦历史上那种真正发生过彻底崩溃的情况要伟大得多。

sentences.en: And then it emerges again as the main city of what becomes the French royal family.
sentences.zh: 然后它再次崛起，成为日后法国王室的主要城市。

sentences.en: So that's really the key, isn't it, Agnes, that it's a royal city from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 所以这才是关键所在，对吧，阿涅丝，它从一开始就是一座王城。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And actually, it's interesting when I say it's the idea, it's as much an idea than a reality.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我说是“概念”时，意思很有趣，它既是一个概念，也是一种现实。

sentences.en: In the 12th century, look at cities all around Europe.
sentences.zh: 在12世纪，看看欧洲各地的城市。

sentences.en: You know, London has 40,000 inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伦敦有4万居民。

sentences.en: Actually, the most populous cities are found in the Flanders and in northern Italy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人口最多的城市在法兰德斯和意大利北部。

sentences.en: Venice and Milan have 200,000 inhabitants, which is enormous.
sentences.zh: 威尼斯和米兰有20万居民，这相当庞大。

sentences.en: But Paris has almost 300,000 inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 但巴黎拥有近30万居民。

sentences.en: And whereas cities usually perform one role, for instance, you know, Ghent, for instance, is a commercial city.
sentences.zh: 通常城市只扮演一种角色，例如，根特是一座商业城市。

sentences.en: Or Venice is a commercial city and Bologna is a university city.
sentences.zh: 或者威尼斯是一座商业城市，博洛尼亚是一座大学城。

sentences.en: Well, Paris performs all the role.
sentences.zh: 然而巴黎扮演了所有的角色。

sentences.en: It's a university city.
sentences.zh: 它是一座大学城。

sentences.en: It's a royal city.
sentences.zh: 它是一座王城。

sentences.en: It's the bishop's city.
sentences.zh: 它是主教之城。

sentences.en: It's also the merchant city.
sentences.zh: 它也是商业之城。

sentences.en: And that time, when actually Notre Dame, it's not a surprise, was built, you know, between, let's say, 1150 and the end of the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 而在那个时期，巴黎圣母院的建造（这并不令人意外）大约在1150年到14世纪末之间，

sentences.en: The end of the 13th century, sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是13世纪末。

sentences.en: Paris has, you know, will live through 150 years of continuous growth.
sentences.zh: 巴黎经历了150年的持续增长。

sentences.en: Imagine that.
sentences.zh: 想象一下。

sentences.en: It's never happened since.
sentences.zh: 此后再也没有发生过。

sentences.en: It's a dream, you know, because we're talking about intellectual expansion, artistic, economic, it's huge, economic boom.
sentences.zh: 这是一个梦想，因为我们谈论的是思想、艺术、经济的扩张，规模极其宏大，经济一片繁荣。

sentences.en: And here you are, you know, this gem of a Gothic masterpiece springing from the very heart, the Ile de la Cité.
sentences.zh: 然后你就看到了这个哥特式杰作的明珠，从其核心西岱岛破土而出。

sentences.en: And at the time, we're talking about 10,000 inhabitants just there.
sentences.zh: 当时，我们仅仅谈论那里就有1万名居民。

sentences.en: Today, there are only, what, not even 900.
sentences.zh: 今天，那里只有，什么来着，连900人都没有。

sentences.en: And it's the bustle of a city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座城市的喧嚣。

sentences.en: It's, you know, life.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活。

sentences.en: The rich live next to the poor and destitute and the narrow lanes.
sentences.zh: 富人与穷人和赤贫者在狭窄的巷子里比邻而居。

sentences.en: I mean, when I had to research that medieval Ile de la Cité, it was extraordinary because it's this, you know, if I was a chemist, I would talk about the precipité of life.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我不得不去查阅关于中世纪西岱岛的资料时，那是极其非凡的，因为如果我是个化学家，我会用“生活的沉淀物”来形容它。

sentences.en: You know, it's there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它就在那里。

sentences.en: And it's coming from all over Europe, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且它来自欧洲各地，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's the other thing, that right from the beginning, Paris is a magnet for people, not just from France, but from across Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是另一回事，从一开始，巴黎就是吸引人们的磁石，不仅来自法国，还来自全欧洲。

sentences.en: And they're going to the university.
sentences.zh: 他们去上大学。

sentences.en: And even in the Middle Ages, Paris is famous for its intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 甚至在中世纪，巴黎就以其知识分子而闻名。

sentences.en: Well, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Dominic's pulling a face.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克在做鬼脸。

sentences.en: That's just my natural resting face, Don.
sentences.zh: 唐，那只是我平常放松时的表情。

sentences.en: Maybe it's a knee-jerk thing when I hear the word intellectuals.
sentences.zh: 也许当我听到“知识分子”这个词时，这是一种条件反射。

sentences.en: You reach for your gun.
sentences.zh: 你就要去拿枪了。

sentences.en: But the students were flocking to the University of Paris and already, because obviously they were students, you know, religious students,
sentences.zh: 但学生们蜂拥至巴黎大学，而且由于他们显然是学生，宗教学生，

sentences.en: but already some very independent-minded scholars and teachers attracting those, you know, young minds of Europe
sentences.zh: 但其中已经有一些思想独立的学者和老师，吸引了欧洲的那些年轻头脑，

sentences.en: and setting up new schools and quite dissident schools right on the left bank.
sentences.zh: 并在左岸建立起新的学校，相当多的异见学校。

sentences.en: And where would the students go and find lodgings?
sentences.zh: 学生们去哪里找住宿呢？

sentences.en: Well, on the left bank.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在左岸。

sentences.en: It wasn't called the left bank, obviously, but because it was cheaper.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时它不叫左岸，但因为那里更便宜。

sentences.en: And you think, OK, well, Jean-Paul Sartre, you know, you can, you can, I mean, it's, it started about...

sentences.zh: 但同样地，巴黎的解放也是……

sentences.zh: 而这正是巴黎圣母院再次登场的时候。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 那是纯粹狂喜的时刻，不仅对巴黎，对全世界都是如此。

sentences.en: This is, in a way, you know, there's, I mean, there are wonderful moments because Paris was not going to be liberated by the Allies.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你知道，这里有，我的意思是，有一些美妙的时刻，因为巴黎并不是由盟军解放的。

sentences.en: Because, you know, as I know, I mean, it was not a strategic...
sentences.zh: 因为，正如我所知，我的意思是，这不是一个战略……

sentences.en: Is it Leclerc?
sentences.zh: 是勒克莱尔吗？

sentences.en: Leclerc.
sentences.zh: 勒克莱尔。

sentences.en: Makes the dash.
sentences.zh: 发起冲锋。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, basically, at some point, you know, in Normandy, as the invasion, or as we call it in France, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，在诺曼底的某个时刻，随着入侵，或者我们在法国所说的，你知道，

sentences.en: Didem, the débarquement is happening, the American troops are not going to go via Paris because it's not strategic.
sentences.zh: D日，登陆正在进行，美军并不打算经由巴黎，因为这不是战略重点。

sentences.en: You know, they have to make their way as fast as possible towards the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们必须以最快的速度向东挺进。

sentences.en: And de Gaulle says, look, guys, we need to liberate Paris.
sentences.zh: 而戴高乐说，听着，伙计们，我们需要解放巴黎。

sentences.en: And so, he has this very heated conversation with Isano.
sentences.zh: 于是，他和艾森豪威尔进行了非常激烈的谈话。

sentences.en: And, of course, the free French are under command of the Americans.
sentences.zh: 当然，自由法国部队是在美军的指挥之下的。

sentences.en: But, because it's so important, Leclerc, who is under the command of General de Gaulle, actually sends a vanguard.
sentences.zh: 但是，由于这件事太重要了，受戴高乐将军指挥的勒克莱尔实际上派出了一个先锋队。

sentences.en: And he faces, really, I mean, he could have been a trial and been a martial court, but he sends a vanguard.
sentences.zh: 他面临着，说实话，他本可能会面临军事法庭的审判，但他还是派出了先锋队。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the resistance in Paris have launched their own insurrection.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，巴黎的抵抗力量已经发起了他们自己的起义。

sentences.en: And there are some very dangerous moments when the peasants don't have anything to eat.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常危急的时刻，市民们甚至没有东西吃。

sentences.en: They obviously, I mean, the resistance can do what they can.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，我的意思是，抵抗力量只能尽其所能。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, adding to the jeopardy is the fact that Hitler has ordered the governor of Paris to basically blow it up.
sentences.zh: 此外，让局势更危险的是，希特勒已经命令巴黎守备长官彻底炸毁这座城市。

sentences.en: Von Toltzens, he has instructions to destroy the city rather than abandon it.
sentences.zh: 冯·霍尔蒂茨（译注：应为冯·肖ltitz），他奉命宁可摧毁这座城市也不将其放弃。

sentences.en: It's the most dramatic, hair-raising narrative.
sentences.zh: 这是最跌宕起伏、惊心动魄的故事。

sentences.en: And then it has this kind of wonderful climax where the governor doesn't blow up Paris.
sentences.zh: 然后它迎来了一个美妙的高潮：守备长官并没有炸毁巴黎。

sentences.en: The Allies join with the free French in capturing it.
sentences.zh: 盟军与自由法国会师并占领了它。

sentences.en: Hemingway gets drunk.
sentences.zh: 海明威喝醉了酒。

sentences.en: And General de Gaulle walks into Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 戴高乐将军走进了巴黎圣母院。

sentences.en: And there is no one better to tell us the story of what then happens than you.
sentences.zh: 没有人比你更适合给我们讲述接下来发生了什么的故事了。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 讲下去吧。

sentences.en: Give us a patriotic French thrill.
sentences.zh: 给我们来点法国式的爱国激情。

sentences.en: So, but Hemingway, you know, before he gets drunk at the Ritz, you know what he does?
sentences.zh: 所以，海明威在丽兹酒店喝醉之前，你知道他做了什么吗？

sentences.zh: 他去了莎士比亚书店去向那里了不起的女士们问好。

sentences.en: And he also calls on his friend Pablo Picasso.
sentences.zh: 他还去拜访了他的朋友巴勃罗·毕加索。

sentences.en: But Pablo is not there.
sentences.zh: 但巴勃罗不在。

sentences.en: And the concierge of Picasso says, do you want to leave a note?
sentences.zh: 毕加索的看门人问，你想留个便条吗？

sentences.en: So he goes back to his Jeep and he takes, you know, hand grenades.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到吉普车上，拿了，你知道的，手榴弹。

sentences.en: And he leaves a few hand grenades with a note to Picasso.
sentences.zh: 他留下了几枚手榴弹和一张写给毕加索的便条。

sentences.en: And then he goes to the Ritz.
sentences.zh: 然后他去了丽兹酒店。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, fast forward 26th of August 1944.
sentences.zh: 现在，时间快进到1944年8月26日。

sentences.en: General de Gaulle has arrived.
sentences.zh: 戴高乐将军已经抵达。

sentences.en: There are still German snipers in the streets of Paris.
sentences.zh: 巴黎街头仍有德国狙击手。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still quite a dangerous place, but obviously, the Leclerc, the Free French and the Americans have, you know, have moved in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里仍然是个相当危险的地方，但显然，勒克莱尔、自由法国和美军，你知道，已经开进城内。

sentences.en: And so that's how the whole day has been conceived.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个一天的构想。

sentences.en: And the radio tells, the French radio tells Parisians and the French that de Gaulle is going to walk down the Champs-Elysees.
sentences.zh: 广播告诉，法国广播电台告诉巴黎人和法国人民，戴高乐将沿着香榭丽舍大街步行前进。

sentences.en: So, two million people in the streets of Paris to acclaim that man they've never seen, really.
sentences.zh: 因此，巴黎街头聚集了两百万人，去欢呼迎接着这位他们从未真正见过的男人。

sentences.en: They might have seen the picture, might have listened to him on the BBC, but they've never met him.
sentences.zh: 他们可能看过照片，可能在BBC上听过他的声音，但他们从未见过他本人。

sentences.en: So, he goes down the Champs-Elysees.
sentences.zh: 于是，他沿着香榭丽舍大街前行。

sentences.en: At the Place de la Concorde, there are far too many people.
sentences.zh: 在协和广场，人实在太多了。

sentences.en: So, he has to hop on a car that drives him through Rue de Rivoli, passes the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 所以他不得不跳上一辆汽车，车子载着他穿过里沃利街，经过卢浮宫。

sentences.en: So, he goes to Hôtel de Ville, where he inspects the troops and the Communist resistance and the Free French all together.
sentences.zh: 然后他前往市政厅，在那里检阅了部队、共产主义抵抗力量以及自由法国的士兵。

sentences.en: And Washington and London and all the film operators are there.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿、伦敦和所有的摄像师都在那里。

sentences.en: And, you know, Washington and London are looking very keenly to see whether de Gaulle is really the man, because they don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，华盛顿和伦敦都在密切关注戴高乐是否真的是合适的人选，因为他们还不知道。

sentences.en: And whether he can tame all those unruly Communist resistance, this is really what they are afraid of, especially Washington.
sentences.zh: 以及他能否驾驭所有那些桀骜不驯的共产主义抵抗力量，这正是他们真正害怕的，尤其是华盛顿。

sentences.en: And de Gaulle being de Gaulle and being a French man, he says, I need to end with a mass, a tidium, at Notre Dame.
sentences.zh: 而戴高乐毕竟是戴高乐，作为一个地道的法国人，他说，我必须在巴黎圣母院以一场弥撒、一场感恩赞歌来收尾。

sentences.en: So, he walks from Hôtel de Ville in the sea of people.
sentences.zh: 于是他从市政厅出发，步入人山人海之中。

sentences.en: And he just passes the porch, the entrance of Notre Dame, when snipers within the cathedral starts shooting.
sentences.zh: 正当他走过巴黎圣母院的门廊和入口时，大教堂内的狙击手开始开枪射击。

sentences.en: And imagine, there are about 10,000 people who have been waiting for de Gaulle to enter.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，大约有一万人一直在等待戴高乐进入。

sentences.en: They've been sitting in the pews everywhere, waiting for their great liberator.
sentences.zh: 他们坐在各处的长椅上，等待着他们伟大的解放者。

sentences.en: And so, how Brex moves.
sentences.zh: 这场景真是太激动人心了。

sentences.en: And we have this audio document that I really urge people to listen to.
sentences.zh: 我们保留了这段音频档案，我强烈敦促大家去听一听。

sentences.en: You can.
sentences.zh: 你们可以听到的。

sentences.en: It's accessible online.
sentences.zh: 它在网上就能找到。

sentences.en: There's this young guy.
sentences.zh: 有一个年轻人。

sentences.en: He's 27.
sentences.zh: 他27岁。

sentences.en: His name is Raymond Marciac.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫雷蒙·马西亚克。

sentences.en: It's his first live reportage for French radio.
sentences.zh: 这是他为法国广播电台做的第一次现场报道。

sentences.en: He's lying on his belly with all his equipment on the upper gallery.
sentences.zh: 他趴在腹部，所有的设备都带在上层看台上。

sentences.en: And we listen to all this.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了这一切。

sentences.en: And he's so, we hear so much fire and the bullets ricketing on the pillars and, you know, such a brouhaha.
sentences.zh: 我们听到密集的枪声，子弹击中石柱的反弹声，你知道，一片喧嚣。

sentences.en: And so, he describes the scene saying that people are just crouching and hiding behind pillars and under the pews.
sentences.zh: 他描述了当时的场景，说人们纷纷蹲下，躲在柱子后面和长椅底下。

sentences.en: And de Gaulle is just walking tall at a slow pace.
sentences.zh: 而戴高乐只是昂首挺胸、迈着缓慢的步伐向前走着。

sentences.en: And the bullets are just whizzing.
sentences.zh: 子弹就在身旁呼啸而过。

sentences.en: And he goes up the altar.
sentences.zh: 他走上了圣坛。

sentences.en: And it's very funny because de Gaulle talks about this moment, obviously, in his memoirs.
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的是，戴高乐在回忆录中显然也提到了这一刻。

sentences.en: And he says, well, I had to be very calm so that people, you know, don't panic.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我必须表现得非常冷静，这样人们才不会恐慌。

sentences.en: Because the last thing we needed was a panic of 10,000 people in that Gothic cathedral.
sentences.zh: 因为我们最不需要的就是这座哥特式大教堂里一万人的集体恐慌。

sentences.en: And he keeps it to 12 minutes, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他把弥撒缩短到了12分钟。

sentences.en: Because, you know, there are a lot of people being injured outside, on the square outside.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，外面广场上有很多人受伤了。

sentences.en: A 12-minute mass.
sentences.zh: 一场12分钟的弥撒。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's Father Ted, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是《泰德神父》里的情节吧？

sentences.en: No, it was a, it was a magnificat.
sentences.zh: 不，那是一首、那是一首谢恩赞歌。

sentences.en: And you can hear it in that audio reportage.
sentences.zh: 你可以在那段音频报道中听到。

sentences.en: It's magnificent.
sentences.zh: 太宏伟了。

sentences.en: And so, he stands up and he walks slowly.
sentences.zh: 然后他站起身，缓缓走去。

sentences.en: And it's quite extraordinary because he could have been shot there.
sentences.zh: 这相当不可思议，因为他当时完全可能被击中。

sentences.en: It was an assassination attempt.
sentences.zh: 这是一次暗杀未遂。

sentences.en: And the, he just has a word with Leclerc and says, you know, clean, clean up the place for me, please.
sentences.zh: 他只是跟勒克莱尔说了句话，说，你知道的，请帮我把这里清理干净。

sentences.en: But to this day, we don't know who those snipers were, whether they were German, collaborators, or perhaps communists.
sentences.zh: 但直到今天，我们都不知道那些狙击手究竟是谁，他们是德国人、维希法国余孽，还是共产主义者。

sentences.en: Because the communists really didn't, didn't want really de Gaulle as the French leaders, the French new leader.
sentences.zh: 因为共产党人其实并不、真的不想让戴高乐成为法国领导人，法国的新领导人。

sentences.en: But luckily, de Gaulle managed to tame the communists.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，戴高乐成功地驯服了共产党人。

sentences.en: And then after the war, do you think that was France, France's, Paris's, do you think that was Paris's last kind of golden age,
sentences.zh: 那么战后，你认为那是法国、法国的、巴黎的，你认为那是巴黎最后的某种黄金时代吗？

sentences.en: the age of the left bank and existentialists, going up to, I don't know, 1968?
sentences.zh: 左岸和存在主义者的时代，一直持续到，我不知道，1968年？

sentences.en: And that was the kind of Paris's last moment in the sun, as it were, internationally.
sentences.zh: 那是巴黎在国际上最后的辉煌时刻，可以说是这样。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, because everybody still at the time could read French or understand French.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，因为当时每个人都还能读懂法语或听懂法语。

sentences.en: So, it means that they didn't need to be read in translation or they were translated.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着他们不需要读翻译本，或者说它们会被翻译。

sentences.en: Whereas today, you don't understand French intellectuals when they speak, and you don't read them because they are not translated.
sentences.zh: 而今天，你听不懂法国知识分子在说什么，你也不读他们的作品，因为它们没有被翻译。

sentences.en: But having said that, I'm not sure that's true, because I think that the influence of Paris intellectuals remains incredibly strong.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我不敢确定这是真的，因为我认为巴黎知识分子的影响力依然极其强大。

sentences.en: I mean, certainly in America.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在美国绝对是这样。

sentences.en: But not as strong as it was in the 50s, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，没有50年代那么强大了。

sentences.en: I think more so.
sentences.zh: 我觉得更有影响力。

sentences.en: I think the influence of Foucault and Derrida is- But that's only in universities, though, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为福柯和德里达的影响是——但那仅限于大学，汤姆。

sentences.en: Yeah, only in universities.
sentences.zh: 对，仅限于大学。

sentences.en: But we've discussed culture wars, and we've seen, you know, this reverberates outwards.
sentences.zh: 但我们讨论过文化战争，而且你知道，我们看到这会向外产生回响。

sentences.en: And the irony is- But you can buy posters of Albert Camus.
sentences.zh: 而讽刺的是——但你可以买到阿尔贝·加缪的海报。

sentences.en: No one can buy- You can't buy a poster of- Because he's-
sentences.zh: 没人能买——你买不到一张——因为他是——

sentences.en: Jack Derrida.
sentences.zh: 雅克·德里达。

sentences.en: He's safe and dead.
sentences.zh: 他已经安全地死去了。

sentences.en: Whereas Foucault and Derrida, I mean, essentially, it's their influence on America that people in Paris are now complaining about.
sentences.zh: 而福柯和德里达，我的意思是，本质上，巴黎人现在正在抱怨的，正是他们在对美国的影响。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说的对。

sentences.en: You know, that's the paradox of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是其中的悖论。

sentences.en: And we would say today that it's because all those American students didn't understand a thing to Derrida and Foucault.
sentences.zh: 我们今天会说，这是因为所有那些美国学生根本没听懂德里达和福柯。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, because deconstruction doesn't mean demolition and doesn't mean consolation.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，解构不等于拆除，也不等于抚慰。

sentences.zh: 所以在翻译过程中有些东西失真了。

sentences.en: But yes, we're suffering today of the terrible misinterpretation of the French thinkers by American students.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我们今天正在遭受美国学生对法国思想家可怕的误读之苦。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢。
